Vitamin D
Vitamin D is derived from both endogenous (skin) and exogenous (diet) sources. The main source of vitamin D for most people is
through exposure to sunlight on the skin containing sufﬁcient ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation. However, the relative contributions of
these two sources are thought to vary widely among individuals and between different geographical areas. In northern latitudes,
there is no UVB radiation of the appropriate wavelength (290–315 nm) for vitamin D synthesis from the end of September to
the end of March; and for the remaining months of the year, 60% of the effective UVB radiation occurs between 11:00 a.m. and
3:00 p.m. The extent of UVB exposure not only depends on the latitude and time, but also cloud cover, ozone, and atmospheric
